channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Hello Houston (February 12, 2026)
item.description: Today: We discuss a local effort to preserve the historic Garden Oaks Theater, talk with a postdoctoral researcher who’s also a Houston Texans cheerleader, break down a new report on pollution in Texas, and more.

item.title: HISD students and parents protest state takeover and ICE operations in Houston
item.description: Thursday’s “sickout” was organized by Community Voices for Public Education, an advocacy group that’s been critical of the district’s state-appointed leadership.

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (February 12, 2026)
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters, we have – The Commuter Cut – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: No tax hike despite budget headache, Whitmire says in State of the City address
item.description: In addition to addressing fiscal challenges, Whitmire unveiled aspirational visions — like a light rail connection to the airport, water taxis on the bayou and giant drainage pipes along I-10.

item.title: Coogs and Brews: Bud Light now offers a University of Houston-branded beer
item.description: UH isn’t the only Texas university Bud Light has crafted a new can for. Bud Light turned burnt orange for the University of Texas at Austin and featured the blue and orange Roadrunner for the University of Texas at San Antonio.

item.title: Galveston, Port Arthur receive $21.8 million in state funding for Arctic icebreaker project
item.description: Officials said the project will create more than 2,400 jobs for the Galveston and Port Arthur communities and invest more than $730 million to grow the business in Texas.

item.title: UH professor refuses to sign indoctrination memo, calling it a ‘red line’
item.description: The memo was issued as a result of Senate Bill 37, an overhaul of the public higher education system passed by the Texas legislature that took effect in September. UH is one of several large state institutions imposing increased authority over course curricula in an attempt to comply with the law.

item.title: ‘You’re being cute:’ Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo walks out during spat over office project
item.description: Hidalgo abruptly left Thursday's commissioners court meeting following a heated discussion about adding an additional safety exit to the office of Commissioner Lesley Briones, which would cut into the office space for Hidalgo's staff.

item.title: Bonck, deZevallos and Pratt lead crowded GOP field vying to succeed Hunt in TX-38
item.description: Texas’ 38th Congressional District was drawn with U.S. Rep. Wesley Hunt in mind. He's vacating the Houston-area seat to run for U.S. Senate.

item.title: Houston ISD unveils plan to shutter 12 schools in 2026-27
item.description: State-appointed Superintendent Mike Miles cited enrollment declines and aging infrastructure as reasons for the proposed closures in Texas’ largest school district.
